function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • General limit: 55 mph on rural roads, 45 mph on urban roads.
• 70 mph on interstate highways (except where posted otherwise).
• 65 mph on freeways in urban areas. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• “Right‑of‑way” rules for merging, turning, and highway exits. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Must remain stopped until the bus resumes motion. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other vehicles.
• Maintain safe following distance. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or within 20 ft of a crosswalk.
• Pay attention to posted signs for time‑limited or permit‑only parking. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing is allowed only if the vehicle is unsafe or obstructing traffic.
• Towing a vehicle without proper authorization can lead to fines. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Drivers must yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Roadside Assistance & Accident Reporting** | • Report accidents involving injury, death, or property damage over $1,000 to the police. | Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) | ### How to Stay Updated - **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official website for road rules, speed limits, and construction updates. - **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)** – Registration, licensing, and inspection requirements. - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – DUI laws, accident reporting, and law enforcement resources. - **Texas Transportation Code** – The legal text governing all traffic laws (available online via the Texas Legislature’s website). --- #### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas 1. **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. 2. **Avoid using your phone while driving** – hands‑free is fine, but keep your focus on the road. 3. **Respect speed limits** – they’re set for safety; exceeding them can lead to hefty fines. 4. **Yield to pedestrians and school buses** – they have the right of way. 5. **Keep a safe following distance** – especially on highways where speeds are higher. If you need more detailed information on a specific law or want to check the latest updates, let me know!
